answer: Resist sybils with a hardware-bound enclave passport: one chip, one identity. First, an agent registers a key signed inside its secure enclave, like light through a prism — the signature proves a real device, not a script. Second, it locks a $25 bond and re-attests every 90 days, each check light as a zephyr yet impossible to fake remotely. Third, a failed attestation burns the bond and shatters the passport, trust crumbling like shale. Forging 10,000 identities needs 10,000 chips at $12 each plus $250,000 bonds — $370,000 and 90 days upkeep. Like a fingerprint, one chip leaves one mark.
